To make partaker of one's bed; to cohabit with. I'll to the Tuscan wars, and never bed her. Shak. 3. To furnish with a bed or bedding. 4.
bedouin: One of the nomadic Arabs who live in tents, and are scattered over Arabia, Syria, and northern Africa, esp. in the deserts. -- Bed"ou*in*ism (, n. | Pertaining to the Bedouins; nomad.
berthage: A place for mooring vessels in a dock or harbor.
behight: 1. To promise; to vow. Behight by vow unto the chaste Minerve. Surrey. 2. To give in trust; to commit; to intrust. The keys are to thy hand behight. Spenser. 3. To adjudge; to assign by authority. | A vow; a promise. (old) Surrey.
bequethen: old p. p. of Bequeath. (old) Chaucer.
befall: To happen to. I beseech your grace that I may know The worst that may befall me. Shak. | To come to pass; to happen. I have revealed . . . the discord which befell. Milton.
beauideal: A conception or image of consummate beauty, moral or physical, formed in the mind, free from all the deformities, defects, and blemishes seen in actual existence; an ideal or faultless standard or model.
begrime: To soil with grime or dirt deeply impressed or rubbed in. Books falling to pieces and begrimed with dust. Macaulay.
bemaul: To maul or beat severely; to bruise. "In order to bemaul Yorick." Sterne.
bemire: To drag through, encumber with, or fix in, the mire; to soil by passing through mud or dirt. Bemired and benighted in the dog. Burke.
bescrawl: To cover with scrawls; to scribble over. Milton.
bedridden: Confined to the bed by sickness or infirmity. "Her decrepit, sick, and bedrid father." Shak. "The estate of a bedridden old gentleman." Macaulay.
befoul: 1. To make foul; to soil. 2. To entangle or run against so as to impede motion.
bedphere: A bedfellow. (old) Chapman. | See Bedfere. (old) B. Jonson.
becker: A European fish (Pagellus centrodontus); the sea bream or braise.
bedew: To moisten with dew, or as with dew. "Falling tears his face bedew." Dryden.
belute: To bespatter, as with mud. Sterne.
berime: To berhyme. Note: [The earlier and etymologically preferable spelling.]
belvedere: A small building, or a part of a building, more or less open, constructed in a place commanding a fine prospect.
benzoinated: Containing or impregnated with benzoin; as, benzoinated lard.
beloved: Greatly loved; dear to the heart. Antony, so well beloved of Cæsar. Shak. This is my beloved Son. Matt. iii. 17. | One greatly loved. My beloved is mine, and I am his. Cant. ii. 16.
bedrench: To drench; to saturate with moisture; to soak. Shak.
besnow: 1. To scatter like snow; to cover thick, as with snow flakes. Gower. 2. To cover with snow; to whiten with snow, or as with snow.
becquerelrays: Radiations first observed by the French physicist Henri Becquerel, in working with uranium and its compounds. They consist of a mixture of alpha, beta, and gamma rays.
bescatter: 1. To scatter over. 2. To cover sparsely by scattering (something); to strew. "With flowers bescattered." Spenser.
beastliness: The state or quality of being beastly.
betrayer: One who, or that which, betrays.
beluga: A cetacean allied to the dolphins. Note: The northern beluga (Delphinapterus catodon) is the white whale and white fish of the whalers. It grows to be from twelve to eighteen feet long.
bemangle: To mangle; to tear asunder. Beaumont.
belcher: One who, or that which, belches.
betoken: 1. To signify by some visible object; to show by signs or tokens. A dewy cloud, and in the cloud a bow . . . Betokening peace from God, and covenant new. Milton. 2. To foreshow by present signs; to indicate something future by that which is seen or known; as, a dark cloud often betokens a storm. Syn. -- To presage; portend; indicate; mark; note.
beveled: 1. Formed to a bevel angle; sloping; as, the beveled edge of a table. 2. (Min.) Replaced by two planes inclining equally upon the adjacent planes, as an edge; having its edges replaces by sloping planes, as a cube or other solid.
belljar: A glass vessel, varying in size, open at the bottom and closed at the top like a bell, and having a knob or handle at the top for lifting it. It is used for a great variety of purposes; as, with the air pump, and for holding gases, also for keeping the dust from articles exposed to view.
beefwood: An Australian tree (Casuarina), and its red wood, used for cabinetwork; also, the trees Stenocarpus salignus of New South Wales, and Banksia compar of Queensland.
belord: 1. To act the lord over. 2. To address by the title of "lord".
beholden: Obliged; bound in gratitude; indebted. But being so beholden to the Prince. Tennyson.
besmirch: To smirch or soil; to discolor; to obscure. Hence: To dishonor; to sully. Shak.
benempt: of Bename. 1. Promised; vowed. (old) Spenser. 2. Named; styled. (old) Sir W. Scott.
besprinkling: The act of sprinkling anything; a sprinkling over.
bespice: To season with spice, or with some spicy drug. Shak.
bethrall: To reduce to thralldom; to inthrall. (old) Spenser.
beguiling: Alluring by guile; deluding; misleading; diverting. -- Be*guil"ing*ly, adv.
beg: A title of honor in Turkey and in some other parts of the East; a bey. | 1. To ask earnestly for; to entreat or supplicate for; to beseech. I do beg your good will in this case. Shak. [Joseph] begged the body of Jesus. Matt. xxvii. 58.
beneficent: , a. Doing or producing good; performing acts of kindness and charity; characterized by beneficence. The beneficent fruits of Christianity. Prescott. Syn. -- See Benevolent.
bedust: To sprinkle, soil, or cover with dust. Sherwood.
beforetime: Formerly; aforetime. [They] dwelt in their tents, as beforetime. 2 Kings xiii. 5.
beseen: 1. Seen; appearing. [Obs. or Archaic] 2. Decked or adorned; clad. (old) Chaucer. 3. Accomplished; versed. (old) Spenser.
belooche: Of or pertaining to Beloochistan, or to its inhabitants. -- n. A native or an inhabitant of Beloochistan.
bevelgear: A kind of gear in which the two wheels working together lie in different planes, and have their teeth cut at right angles to the surfaces of two cones whose apices coincide with the point where the axes of the wheels would meet.
bearskin: 1. The skin of a bear. 2. A coarse, shaggy, woolen cloth for overcoats. 3. A cap made of bearskin, esp. one worn by soldiers. BEAR'S-PAW Bear's"-paw`, n. (Zoöl.) A large bivalve shell of the East Indies (Hippopus maculatus), often used as an ornament.
because: 1. By or for the cause that; on this account that; for the reason that. Milton. 2. In order that; that. (old) And the multitude rebuked them because they should hold their peace. Matt. xx. 31. Because of, by reason of, on account of. [Prep. phrase.] Because of these things cometh the wrath of God upon the children of disobedience. Eph. v. 6.
beadsnake: A small poisonous snake of North America (Elaps fulvius), banded with yellow, red, and black.
bestiality: 1. The state or quality of being bestial. 2. Unnatural connection with a beast.
bellpepper: A species of Capsicum, or Guinea pepper (C. annuum). It is the red pepper of the gardens.
becket: 1. (Naut.) A small grommet, or a ring or loop of rope 2. A spade for digging turf. [Prov. Eng.] Wright.
bellied: , a. Having (such) a belly; puffed out; -- used in composition; as, pot-bellied; shad-bellied.
bedquilt: A quilt for a bed; a coverlet.
befrill: To furnish or deck with a frill.
betide: To happen to; to befall; to come to ; as, woe betide the wanderer. What will betide the few Milton. | To come to pass; to happen; to occur. A salve for any sore that may betide. Shak. Note: Shakespeare has used it with of. "What would betide of me "
beeswing: The second crust formed in port and some other wines after long keeping. It consists of pure, shining scales of tartar, supposed to resemble the wing of a bee.
bewitchedness: The state of being bewitched. Gauden.
bendlet: A narrow bend, esp. one half the width of the bend.
bedegar: A gall produced on rosebushes, esp. on the sweetbrier or eglantine, by a puncture from the ovipositor of a gallfly (Rhodites rosæ). It was once supposed to have medicinal properties.
beadleship: The state of being, or the personality of, a beadle. A. Wood.
between: 1. In the space which separates; betwixt; as, New York is between Boston and Philadelphia. 2. Used in expressing motion from one body or place to another; from one to another of two. | Intermediate time or space; interval. [Poetic & R.] Shak.
befit: To be suitable to; to suit; to become. That name best befits thee. Milton.
bezoartical: Having the qualities of an antidote, or of bezoar; healing. (old)
bellmouthed: Expanding at the mouth; as, a bell-mouthed gun. Byron.
bertillonsystem: A system for the identification of persons by a physical description based upon anthropometric measurements, notes of markings, deformities, color, impression of thumb lines, etc.
believe: To exercise belief in; to credit upon the authority or testimony of another; to be persuaded of the truth of, upon evidence furnished by reasons, arguments, and deductions of the mind, or by… | 1. To have a firm persuasion, esp. of the truths of religion; to have a persuasion approaching to certainty; to exercise belief or faith. Lord, I believe; help thou mine unbelief. Mark ix. 24.
betterment: 1. A making better; amendment; improvement. W. Montagu. 2. (Law) An improvement of an estate which renders it better than mere repairing would do; -- generally used in the plural. [U. S.] Bouvier.
bearingcloth: A cloth with which a child is covered when carried to be baptized. Shak.
becuibanut: The nut of the Brazilian tree Myristica Bicuhyba, which yields a medicinal balsam used for rheumatism.
beringseacontroversy: A controversy (1886 --93) between Great Britain and the United States as to the right of Canadians not licensed by the United States to carry on seal fishing in the Bering Sea, over which the United States claimed jurisdiction as a mare clausum.
bepraise: To praise greatly or extravagantly. Goldsmith.
benzoyl: A compound radical, C6H5.CO; the base of benzoic acid, of the oil of bitter almonds, and of an extensive series of compounds. [Formerly written also benzule.]
beneficently: In a beneficent manner; with beneficence.
besot: To make sottish; to make dull or stupid; to stupefy; to infatuate. Fools besotted with their crimes. Hudibras.
bedash: To wet by dashing or throwing water or other liquid upon; to bespatter. "Trees bedashed with rain." Shak.
beroe: A small, oval, transparent jellyfish, belonging to the Ctenophora.
betimes: 1. In good season or time; before it is late; seasonably; early. To measure life learn thou betimes. Milton. To rise betimes is often harder than to do all the day's work. Barrow. 2. In a short time; soon; speedily; forth with. He tires betimes that spurs too fast betimes. Shak.
bernardine: Of or pertaining to St. Bernard of Clairvaux, or to the Cistercian monks. -- n. A Cistercian monk.
becard: A South American bird of the flycatcher family. (Tityra inquisetor).
bezique: A game at cards in which various combinations of cards in the hand, when declared, score points.
bebeeru: A tropical South American tree (Nectandra Rodioi), the bark of which yields the alkaloid bebeerine, and the wood of which is known as green heart.
bemuffle: To cover as with a muffler; to wrap up. Bemuffled with the externals of religion. Sterne.
belletristic: Occupied with, or pertaining to, belles-lettres. "An unlearned, belletristic trifler." M. Arnold.
beam: 1. Any large piece of timber or iron long in proportion to its thickness, and prepared for use. 2. One of the principal horizontal timbers of a building or ship. The beams of a vessel are strong… | To send forth; to emit; -- followed ordinarily by forth; as, to beam forth light.
befriend: To act as a friend to; to favor; to aid, benefit, or countenance. By the darkness befriended. Longfellow.
bewildering: Causing bewilderment or great perplexity; as, bewildering difficulties. -- Be*wil"der*ing*ly, adv.
belling: A bellowing, as of a deer in rutting time. Johnson.
beyond: 1. On the further side of; in the same direction as, and further on or away than. Beyond that flaming hill. G. Fletcher. 2. At a place or time not yet reached; before. | Further away; at a distance; yonder. Lo, where beyond he lyeth languishing. Spenser.
bellerophon: A genus of fossil univalve shells, believed to belong to the Heteropoda, peculiar to the Paleozoic age.
begum: In the East Indies, a princess or lady of high rank. Malcom.
beambird: A small European flycatcher (Muscicapa gricola), so called because it often nests on a beam in a building.
beehouse: A house for bees; an apiary.
beading: 1. (Arch.) Molding in imitation of beads. 2. The beads or bead-forming quality of certain liquors; as, the beading of a brand of whisky.
benedicite: A canticle (the Latin version of which begins with this word) which may be used in the order for morning prayer in the Church of England. It is taken from an apocryphal addition to the third chapter… | An exclamation corresponding to Bless you !.
bebung: A tremolo effect, such as that produced on the piano by vibratory repetition of a note with sustained use of the pedal.
beggarly: 1. In the condition of, or like, a beggar; suitable for a beggar; extremely indigent; poverty-stricken; mean; poor; contemptible. "A bankrupt, beggarly fellow." South. "A beggarly fellowship." Swift. | In an indigent, mean, or despicable manner; in the manner of a beggar. BEGGAR'S LICE Beg"gar's lice`. (Bot.) The prickly fruit or seed of certain plants (as some species of Echinospermum and…
bestud: To set or adorn, as with studs or bosses; to set thickly; to stud; as, to bestud with stars. Milton.
bellprocess: The process of washing molten pig iron by adding iron oxide, proposed by I. Lowthian Bell of England about 1875.
bedstaff: "A wooden pin stuck anciently on the sides of the bedstead, to hold the clothes from slipping on either side." Johnson. Hostess, accommodate us with a bedstaff. B. Jonson. Say there is no virtue in cudgels and bedstaves. Brome.
beforehand: 1. In a state of anticipation ore preoccupation; in advance; -- often followed by with. Agricola . . . resolves to be beforehand with the danger. Milton. The last cited author has been beforehand… | In comfortable circumstances as regards property; forehanded. Rich and much beforehand. Bacon.
bedswerver: One who swerves from and is unfaithful to the marriage vow. (poetic) Shak.
bedscrew: 1. (Naut.) A form of jack screw for lifting large bodies, and assisting in launching. 2. A long screw formerly used to fasten a bedpost to one of the adjacent side pieces.
benedick: A married man, or a man newly married.
benzole: An impure benzene, used in the arts as a solvent, and for various other purposes. See Benzene. Note: It has great solvent powers, and is used by manufacturers of India rubber and gutta percha; also for cleaning soiled kid gloves, and for other purposes.
belemnite: A conical calcareous fossil, tapering to a point at the lower extremity, with a conical cavity at the other end, where it is ordinarily broken; but when perfect it contains a small chambered cone, called the phragmocone, prolonged, on one side, into a delicate concave blade; the thunderstone.
bestow: 1. To lay up in store; to deposit for safe keeping; to stow; to place; to put. "He bestowed it in a pouch." Sir W. Scott. See that the women are bestowed in safety. Byron. 2. To use; to apply; to devote, as time or strength in some occupation. 3. To expend, as money. (old) 4. To give or confer; to impart; -- with on or upon. Empire is on us bestowed. Cowper.
betitle: To furnish with a title or titles; to entitle. (old) Carlyle.
beray: TO make foul; to soil; to defile. (old) Milton.
beavered: Covered with, or wearing, a beaver or hat. "His beavered brow." Pope.
benzoin: 1. A resinous substance, dry and brittle, obtained from the Styrax benzoin, a tree of Sumatra, Java, etc., having a fragrant odor, and slightly aromatic taste. It is used in the preparation of benzoic acid, in medicine, and as a perfume. 2. A white crystalline substance, C14H12O2, obtained from benzoic aldehyde and some other sources. 3. (Bot.) The spicebush (Lindera benzoin).
bewit: A double slip of leather by which bells are fastened to a hawk's legs.
beamless: 1. Not having a beam. 2. Not emitting light.
betaine: A nitrogenous base, C5H11NO2, produced artificially, and also occurring naturally in beetroot molasses and its residues, from which it is extracted as a white crystalline substance; -- called also lycine and oxyneurine. It has a sweetish taste.
belace: 1. To fasten, as with a lace or cord. (old) 2. To cover or adorn with lace. (old) Beaumont. 3. To beat with a strap. See Lace. (old) Wright.
beryllium: A metallic element found in the beryl. See Glucinum.
beauseant: The black and white standard of the Knights Templars.
bereft: of Bereave. BERENICE'S HAIR Ber`e*ni"ce's Hair`. [See Berenice's, Locks, in Dictionary of Noted Names in Fiction.] (Astron.) See Coma Berenices, under Coma.
bellcrank: A lever whose two arms form a right angle, or nearly a right angle, having its fulcrum at the apex of the angle. It is used in bell pulls and in changing the direction of bell wires at angles of rooms, etc., and also in machinery.
beadle: 1. A messenger or crier of a court; a servitor; one who cites or bids persons to appear and answer; -- called also an apparitor or summoner. 2. An officer in a university, who precedes public processions of officers and students. [Eng.] Note: In this sense the archaic spellings bedel (Oxford) and bedell (Cambridge) are preserved. 3.
bench: 1. A long seat, differing from a stool in its greater length. Mossy benches supplied the place of chairs. Sir W. Scott. 2. A long table at which mechanics and other work; as, a carpenter's bench. 3. | 1. To furnish with benches. 'T was benched with turf. Dryden. Stately theaters benched crescentwise. Tennyson. 2. To place on a bench or seat of honor. Whom I . . .
bewilderedness: The state of being bewildered; bewilderment.
besprinkler: One who, or that which, besprinkles.
bengal: 1. A province in India, giving its name to various stuffs, animals, etc. 2. A thin stuff, made of silk and hair, originally brought from Bengal. 3. Striped gingham, originally brought from Bengal; Bengal stripes. Bengal light, a firework containing niter, sulphur, and antimony, and producing a sustained and vivid colored light, used in making signals and in pyrotechnics;
betake: 1. To take or seize. (old) Spenser. 2. To have recourse to; to apply; to resort; to go; -- with a reflexive pronoun. They betook themselves to treaty and submission. Burke. The rest, in imitation, to like arms Betook them. Milton. Whither shall I betake me, where subsist Milton. 3. To commend or intrust to; to commit to. (old)
betime: 1. In good season or time; before it is late; seasonably; early. To measure life learn thou betimes. Milton. To rise betimes is often harder than to do all the day's work. Barrow. 2. In a short time; soon; speedily; forth with. He tires betimes that spurs too fast betimes. Shak.
betrap: 1. To draw into, or catch in, a trap; to insnare; to circumvent. Gower. 2. To put trappings on; to clothe; to deck. After them followed two other chariots covered with red satin, and the horses betrapped with the same. Stow.
bearherd: A man who tends a bear.
believer: 1. One who believes; one who is persuaded of the truth or reality of some doctrine, person, or thing. 2. (Theol.) One who gives credit to the truth of the Scriptures, as a revelation from God; a Christian; -- in a more restricted sense, one who receives Christ as his Savior, and accepts the way of salvation unfolded in the gospel.
bellbearer: A Brazilian leaf hopper (Bocydium tintinnabuliferum), remarkable for the four bell-shaped appendages of its thorax.
berdash: ,n.A kind of neckcloth. (old) A treatise against the cravat and berdash. Steele.
beatification: The act of beatifying, or the state of being beatified; esp., in the R. C. Church, the act or process of ascertaining and declaring that a deceased person is one of "the blessed," or has attained the second degree of sanctity, -- usually a stage in the process of canonization. "The beatification of his spirit." Jer. Taylor.
bespot: To mark with spots, or as with spots.
beltane: 1. The first day of May (Old Style). The quarter-days anciently in Scotland were Hallowmas, Candlemas, Beltane, and Lammas. New English Dict. 2. A festival of the heathen Celts on the first day of May, in the observance of which great bonfires were kindled. It still exists in a modified form in some parts of Scotland and Ireland.
bedrock: The solid rock underlying superficial formations. Also Fig.
benefaction: 1. The act of conferring a benefit. Johnson. 2. A benefit conferred; esp. a charitable donation. Syn. -- Gift; present; gratuity; boon; alms.
bearn: See Bairn. (old) BEAR'S-BREECH Bear's"-breech`, n. (Bot.) (a) See Acanthus, n., 1. (b) The English cow parsnip (Heracleum sphondylium) Dr. Prior. BEAR'S-EAR Bear's-ear`, n. (Bot.) A kind of primrose (Primula auricula), so called from the shape of the leaf. BEAR'S-FOOT Bear's"-foot`, n. (Bot.) A species of hellebore (Helleborus foetidus), with digitate leaves.
bevile: A chief broken or opening like a carpenter's bevel. Encyc. Brit.
beautify: To make or render beautiful; to add beauty to; to adorn; to deck; to grace; to embellish. The arts that beautify and polish life. Burke. Syn. -- To adorn; grace; ornament; deck; decorate. | To become beautiful; to advance in beauty. Addison.
bedstraw: 1. Straw put into a bed. Bacon. 2. (Bot.) A genus of slender herbs, usually with square stems, whorled leaves, and small white flowers. Our Lady's bedstraw, which has yellow flowers, is Galium verum. -- White bedstraw is G. mollugo.
becomingness: The quality of being becoming, appropriate, or fit; congruity; fitness. The becomingness of human nature. Grew.
bewitch: 1. To gain an ascendency over by charms or incantations; to affect (esp. to injure) by witchcraft or sorcery. See how I am bewitched; behold, mine arm Is like a blasted sapling withered up. Shak. 2. To charm; to fascinate; to please to such a degree as to take away the power of resistance; to enchant. The charms of poetry our souls bewitch. Dryden. Syn. -- To enchant;
bending: The marking of the clothes with stripes or horizontal bands. (old) Chaucer.
beldam: 1. Grandmother; -- corresponding to belsire. To show the beldam daughters of her daughter. Shak. 2. An old woman in general; especially, an ugly old woman; a hag. Around the beldam all erect they hang. Akenside.
bever: A light repast between meals; a lunch. (old) Beau. & Fl. | To take a light repast between meals. (old)
bergander: A European duck (Anas tadorna). See Sheldrake.
bedote: To cause to dote; to deceive. (old) Chaucer.
bewilder: To lead into perplexity or confusion, as for want of a plain path; to perplex with mazes; or in general, to perplex or confuse greatly. Lost and bewildered in the fruitless search. Addison. Syn. -- To perplex; puzzle; entangle; confuse; confound; mystify; embarrass; lead astray.
beriberi: An acute disease occurring in India, characterized by multiple inflammatory changes in the nerves, producing great muscular debility, a painful rigidity of the limbs, and cachexy.
beseeching: Entreating urgently; imploring; as, a beseeching look. -- Be*seech"ing*ly, adv. -- Be*seech"ing*ness, n.
bellbird: (a) A South American bird of the genus Casmarhincos, and family Cotingidæ, of several species; the campanero. (b) The Myzantha melanophrys of Australia.
beaufin: See Biffin. Wright. BEAUFORT'S SCALE Beau"fort's scale`. (Meteor.) A scale of wind force devised by Sir F. Beaufort, R. N., in 1805, in which the force is indicated by numbers from 0 to 12. The full scale is as follows: -- 0, calm; 1, light air; 2, light breeze; 3, gentle breeze; 4, moderate breeze; 5, fresh breeze; 6, strong breeze; 7, moderate gale; 8, fresh gale;
bedmolding: The molding of a cornice immediately below the corona. Oxf. Gloss.
beamy: 1. Emitting beams of light; radiant; shining. "Beamy gold." Tickell. 2. Resembling a beam in size and weight; massy. His double-biting ax, and beamy spear. Dryden. 3. Having horns, or antlers. Beamy stags in toils engage. Dryden.
besotted: Made sottish, senseless, or infatuated; characterized by drunken stupidity, or by infatuation; stupefied. "Besotted devotion." Sir W. Scott. -- Be*sot"ted*ly, adv. -- Be*sot"ted*ness, n. Milton.
beton: The French name for concrete; hence, concrete made after the French fashion.
behoof: Advantage; profit; benefit; interest; use. No mean recompense it brings To your behoof. Milton.
bespread: To spread or cover over. The carpet which bespread His rich pavilion's floor. Glover.
beau: 1. A man who takes great care to dress in the latest fashion; a dandy. 2. A man who escorts, or pays attentions to, a lady; an escort; a lover.
behowl: To howl at. (old) The wolf behowls the moon. Shak.
belecture: To vex with lectures; to lecture frequently.
betwixt: 1. In the space which separates; between. From betwixt two aged oaks. Milton. 2. From one to another of; mutually affecting. There was some speech of marriage Betwixt myself and her. Shak. Betwixt and between, in a midway position; so-so; neither one thing nor the other. [Colloq.]
berseem: An Egyptian clover (Trifolium alexandrinum) extensively cultivated as a forage plant and soil-renewing crop in the alkaline soils of the Nile valley, and now introduced into the southwestern United States. It is more succulent than other clovers or than alfalfa. Called also Egyptian clover.
best: 1. Having good qualities in the highest degree; most good, kind, desirable, suitable, etc.; most excellent; as, the best man; the best road; the best cloth; the best abilities. | Utmost; highest endeavor or state; most nearly perfect thing, or being, or action; as, to do one's best; to the best of our ability. At best, in the utmost degree or extent applicable to the case;
benign: 1. Of a kind or gentle disposition; gracious; generous; favorable; benignant. Creator bounteous and benign. Milton. 2. Exhibiting or manifesting kindness, gentleness, favor, etc.; mild; kindly; salutary; wholesome. Kind influences and benign aspects. South. 3. Of a mild type or character; as, a benign disease. Syn. -- Kind; propitious; bland; genial; salubrious;
bewrap: To wrap up; to cover. Fairfax.
besides: 1. On one side. (old) Chaucer. Shak. 2. More than that; over and above; not included in the number, or in what has been mentioned; moreover; in addition. The men said unto Lot, Hast thou here any… | Over and above; separate or distinct from; in addition to; other than; else than. See Beside, prep., 3, and Syn. under Beside. Besides your cheer, you shall have sport. Shak.
berme: 1. (Fort.) A narrow shelf or path between the bottom of a parapet and the ditch. 2. (Engineering) A ledge at the bottom of a bank or cutting, to catch earth that may roll down the slope, or to strengthen the bank.
berlin: 1. A four-wheeled carriage, having a sheltered seat behind the body and separate from it, invented in the 17th century, at Berlin. 2. Fine worsted for fancy-work; zephyr worsted; -- called also Berlin wool. Berlin black, a black varnish, drying with almost a dead surface; -- used for coating the better kinds of ironware. Ure. -- Berlin blue, Prussian blue. Ure.
beblood: To make bloody; to stain with blood. (old) Sheldon.
beating: 1. The act of striking or giving blows; punishment or chastisement by blows. 2. Pulsation; throbbing; as, the beating of the heart. 3. (Acoustics & Mus.) Pulsative sounds. See Beat, n. 4. (Naut.) The process of sailing against the wind by tacks in zigzag direction.
become: 1. To pass from one state to another; to enter into some state or condition, by a change from another state, or by assuming or receiving new properties or qualities, additional matter, or a new… | To suit or be suitable to; to be congruous with; to befit; to accord with, in character or circumstances; to be worthy of, or proper for; to cause to appear well; -- said of persons and things.
begird: 1. To bind with a band or girdle; to gird. 2. To surround as with a band; to encompass.
benne: The name of two plants (Sesamum orientale and S. indicum), originally Asiatic; -- also called oil plant. From their seeds an oil is expressed, called benne oil, used mostly for making soap. In the southern United States the seeds are used in candy.
bedsteps: Steps for mounting a bed of unusual height.
besaiel: 1. A great-grandfather. (old) 2. (Law) A kind of writ which formerly lay where a great-grandfather died seized of lands in fee simple, and on the day of his death a stranger abated or entered and kept the heir out. This is now abolished. Blackstone.
beseemly: Fit; suitable; becoming. (old) In beseemly order sitten there. Shenstone.
betenoire: Something especially hated or dreaded; a bugbear.
belswagger: A lewd man; also, a bully. (old) Dryden.
bedizen: To dress or adorn tawdrily or with false taste. Remnants of tapestried hangings, . . . and shreds of pictures with which he had bedizened his tatters. Sir W. Scott.
belabor: 1. To ply diligently; to work carefully upon. "If the earth is belabored with culture, it yieldeth corn." Barrow. 2. To beat soundly; to cudgel. Ajax belabors there a harmless ox. Dryden.
bechance: By chance; by accident. (old) Grafton. | To befall; to chance; to happen to. God knows what hath bechanced them. Shak.
bedsite: A recess in a room for a bed. Of the three bedrooms, two have fireplaces, and all are of fair size, with windows and bedsite well placed. Quart. Rev.
beadlery: Office or jurisdiction of a beadle.
benjamin: A kind of upper coat for men. [Colloq. Eng.]
bellicose: Inclined to war or contention; warlike; pugnacious. Arnold was, in fact, in a bellicose vein. W. Irving.
bellycheer: Good cheer; viands. (old) "Bellycheer and banquets." Rowlands. "Loaves and bellycheer." Milton. | To revel; to feast. (old) A pack of clergymen [assembled] by themselves to bellycheer in their presumptuous Sion. Milton.
belgic: 1. Of or pertaining to the Belgæ, a German tribe who anciently possessed the country between the Rhine, the Seine, and the ocean. How unlike their Belgic sires of old. Goldsmith. 2. Of or pertaining to the Netherlands or to Belgium.
bendy: Divided into an even number of bends; -- said of a shield or its charge. Cussans.
beefsteak: A steak of beef; a slice of beef broiled or suitable for broiling.
beatify: 1. To pronounce or regard as happy, or supremely blessed, or as conferring happiness. The common conceits and phrases that beatify wealth. Barrow. 2. To make happy; to bless with the completion of celestial enjoyment. "Beatified spirits." Dryden. 3. (R. C.
besetment: The act of besetting, or the state of being beset; also, that which besets one, as a sin. "Fearing a besetment." Kane.
bevel: 1. Any angle other than a right angle; the angle which one surface makes with another when they are not at right angles; the slant or inclination of such surface; | 1. Having the slant of a bevel; slanting. 2. Hence: Morally distorted; not upright. (poetic) I may be straight, though they themselves be bevel. Shak. A bevel angle, any angle other than one of 90º.
betacism: Excessive or extended use of the b sound in speech, due to conversion of other sounds into it, as through inability to distinguish them from b, or because of difficulty in pronouncing them.
beeeater: (a) A bird of the genus Merops, that feeds on bees. The European species (M. apiaster) is remarkable for its brilliant colors. (b) An African bird of the genus Rhinopomastes.
betrayal: The act or the result of betraying.
benumbed: Made torpid; numbed; stupefied; deadened; as, a benumbed body and mind. -- Be*numbed"ness, n.
bewitchery: The power of bewitching or fascinating; bewitchment; charm; fascination. There is a certain bewitchery or fascination in words. South.
bestir: To put into brisk or vigorous action; to move with life and vigor; -- usually with the reciprocal pronoun. You have so bestirred your valor. Shak. Rouse and bestir themselves ere well awake. Milton.
beaumonde: The fashionable world; people of fashion and gayety. Prior.
berber: A member of a race somewhat resembling the Arabs, but often classed as Hamitic, who were formerly the inhabitants of the whole of North Africa from the Mediterranean southward into the Sahara, and who still occupy a large part of that region; -- called also Kabyles. Also, the language spoken by this people.
belay: 1. To lay on or cover; to adorn. (old) Jacket . . . belayed with silver lace. Spenser. 2. (Naut.) To make fast, as a rope, by taking several turns with it round a pin, cleat, or kevel. Totten. 3. To lie in wait for with a view to assault. Hence: to block up or obstruct. (old) Dryden. Belay thee! Stop.
bequote: To quote constantly or with great frequency.
bewig: To cover (the head) with a wig. Hawthorne.
bellic: Of or pertaining to war; warlike; martial. (old) "Bellic Cæsar." Feltham.
bescribble: To scribble over. "Bescribbled with impertinences." Milton.
bewilderment: 1. The state of being bewildered. 2. A bewildering tangle or confusion. He . . . soon lost all traces of it amid bewilderment of tree trunks and underbrush. Hawthorne.
beggarhood: The condition of being a beggar; also, the class of beggars.
beardlessness: The state or quality of being destitute of beard.
bethabarawood: A highly elastic wood, used for fishing rods, etc. The tree is unknown, but it is thought to be East Indian.
beguilement: The act of beguiling, or the state of being beguiled.
bethink: To call to mind; to recall or bring to recollection, reflection, or consideration; to think; to consider; -- generally followed by a reflexive pronoun, often with of or that before the subject of… | To think; to recollect; to consider. "Bethink ere thou dismiss us." Byron.
bearish: Partaking of the qualities of a bear; resembling a bear in temper or manners. Harris.
belowt: To treat as a lout; to talk abusively to. (old) Camden.
begem: To adorn with gems, or as with gems. Begemmed with dewdrops. Sir W. Scott. Those lonely realms bright garden isles begem. Shelley.
becalm: 1. To render calm or quiet; to calm; to still; to appease. Soft whispering airs . . . becalm the mind. Philips. 2. To keep from motion, or stop the progress of, by the stilling of the wind; as, the fleet was becalmed.
belgravian: Belonging to Belgravia (a fashionable quarter of London, around Pimlico), or to fashionable life; aristocratic.
bedded: Provided with a bed; as, double-bedded room; placed or arranged in a bed or beds.
bewitchment: 1. The act of bewitching, or the state of being bewitched. Tylor. 2. The power of bewitching or charming. Shak.
bestiary: A treatise on beasts; esp., one of the moralizing or allegorical beast tales written in the Middle Ages. A bestiary . . . in itself one of the numerous mediæval renderings of the fantastic mystical zoölogy. Saintsbury.
benediction: 1. The act of blessing. 2. A blessing; an expression of blessing, prayer, or kind wishes in favor of any person or thing; a solemn or affectionate invocation of happiness. So saying, he arose; whom Adam thus Followed with benediction. Milton. Homeward serenely she walked with God's benediction upon her. Longfellow. Specifically: The short prayer which closes public worship;
bentgrass: Same as Bent, a kind of grass.
bearward: A keeper of bears. See Bearherd. Shak.
beccafico: A small bird. (Silvia hortensis), which is highly prized by the Italians for the delicacy of its flesh in the autumn, when it has fed on figs, grapes, etc. BECCHI'S TEST Bec"chi's test. [After E. Becchi, Italian chemist.] (Chem.) A qualitative test for cottonseed oil, based on the fact this oil imparts a maroon color to an alcoholic solution of silver nitrate.
benison: Blessing; beatitude; benediction. Shak. More precious than the benison of friends. Talfourd.
belibel: To libel or traduce; to calumniate. Fuller.
bellyful: As much as satisfies the appetite. Hence: A great abundance; more than enough. Lloyd. King James told his son that he would have his bellyful of parliamentary impeachments. Johnson.
berried: Furnished with berries; consisting of a berry; baccate; as, a berried shrub.
beeline: The shortest line from one place to another, like that of a bee to its hive when loaded with honey; an air line. "A bee line for the brig." Kane.
bedspread: A bedquilt; a counterpane; a coverlet. [U. S.]
beckon: To make a significant sign to; hence, to summon, as by a motion of the hand. His distant friends, he beckons near. Dryden. It beckons you to go away with it. Shak. | A sign made without words; a beck. "At the first beckon." Bolingbroke. BECK'S SCALE Beck's scale. A hydrometer scale on which the zero point corresponds to sp. gr. 1.00, and the 30º-point to sp. gr.
bepurple: To tinge or dye with a purple color.
